name: Barcelona
tagline: From the 1786 Gothic Quarter to the vermouth bar that won over Anthony Bourdain — the Spanish city with the most Michelin stars.

Can Culleretes.description: Barcelona's oldest restaurant, open since 1786 in the heart of the Gothic Quarter. Its walls are covered with photos of a century of famous diners.

Disfrutar.description: Named the world's best restaurant in 2024 by The World's 50 Best. Avant-garde cuisine from three elBulli alumni.

Quimet & Quimet.description: A family-run 1914 bodega in Poble Sec — five generations serving montaditos standing at the bar. Anthony Bourdain visited on 'No Reservations' during his Spain episode.

La Cova Fumada.description: A 1944 fishermen's tavern in Barceloneta, birthplace of the legendary "bomba" with potato and meat.

Enigma.description: Albert Adrià's most secretive project, with a reservation that's nearly impossible to get. Two Michelin stars.

Els 4 Gats.description: The 1897 café-cabaret where a young Picasso designed the menu. A historic gathering place for Catalan Modernisme.

ABaC.description: Jordi Cruz's haute cuisine inside a boutique hotel in Sant Gervasi. Three Michelin stars.

Cocina Hermanos Torres.description: The Torres twins' workshop-restaurant, with the kitchen itself as the central stage. Three Michelin stars.

Lasarte.description: Martín Berasategui's Barcelona venture, with Paolo Casagrande leading the kitchen. Three Michelin stars.

Mont Bar.description: A chef-driven tapas counter with the soul of a neighborhood bar — and two Michelin stars, unusual for the format.

Cinc Sentits.description: A sensory, farm-to-table tasting menu in the heart of the Eixample. Two Michelin stars.

Alkimia.description: Catalan cuisine distilled to its essence by Jordi Vilà. One Michelin star.

Dos Palillos.description: Asian tapas from Albert Raurich, former head chef at elBulli. One Michelin star.

Koy Shunka.description: Japanese cuisine with a Catalan accent, steps from the Cathedral. One Michelin star.

Via Veneto.description: A classic of Catalan haute cuisine since 1967, complete with a tableside flambéed dessert cart. One Michelin star.

Enoteca Paco Pérez.description: Paco Pérez's sea-driven cuisine with Mediterranean views from the Hotel Arts. Two Michelin stars.

Mercat de la Boqueria.description: Barcelona's most-visited market, just off Las Ramblas, with stalls of ham, cut fruit and fresh seafood.

Moments.description: The restaurant of the Mandarin Oriental Hotel, led by Raül Balam Ruscalleda, son of Carme Ruscalleda. Avant-garde Catalan cuisine with two Michelin stars.

Caelis.description: French-rooted haute cuisine inside Hotel El Palace, led by chef Romain Fornell. One Michelin star.

Angle.description: Fine dining from Jordi Cruz inside Hotel Cram, in the Eixample district. One Michelin star.

Hisop.description: Seasonal, technique-driven cuisine led by Oriol Ivern in Sant Gervasi. One Michelin star.

Hofmann.description: Restaurant tied to the cooking school founded by Mey Hofmann in 1982, now run by her daughter Silvia. One Michelin star.

Xerta.description: Fran López's Ebro Delta cuisine inside Hotel Ohla Eixample, built around exceptional rice dishes. One Michelin star.

MAE Barcelona.description: Mediterranean and Latin American-rooted cuisine in Sant Gervasi, with two tasting menus. Earned its first Michelin star in 2025.

Nectari.description: Market-driven tasting menus at a relatively accessible price for a starred restaurant, by chef Jordi Esteve. One Michelin star.

Quirat.description: Contemporary, seasonal Catalan cuisine from chef Víctor Torres, in Gràcia. One Michelin star.

Brabo.description: A contemporary grill house focused on fire-cooked meat and fish, from Rafa Panatieri and Jorge Sastre in Barceloneta. One Michelin star.

Bardeni-Caldeni.description: A meat-focused counter from butcher-chef Dani Lechuga near Sagrada Família, specializing in native cattle breeds. Bib Gourmand.

Berbena.description: Relaxed, ever-changing market cuisine in Gràcia, recognized with a Bib Gourmand for its value for money.

Oníric.description: Affordable chef-driven cuisine in Gràcia, added to the Bib Gourmand list in the 2026 guide.

Saó.description: Seasonal, product-driven cooking in a small Gràcia dining room, awarded a Bib Gourmand.

Avenir.description: A neighborhood restaurant in Sant Gervasi with honest market cooking, awarded a Bib Gourmand.

Cruix.description: Good-value seasonal cooking in the Eixample, included in the Michelin Guide's Bib Gourmand.

Glug.description: A small market-driven restaurant in Eixample Esquerra, awarded a Bib Gourmand.

Bacaro.description: Tucked beside the Boqueria market, it serves casual Venetian small plates in the cicchetti style. Bib Gourmand.

Fismuler.description: The Barcelona outpost of Madrid's acclaimed Fismuler, built on seasonal, product-driven cooking. Bib Gourmand.

7 Portes.description: Open since 1836 next to Pla de Palau, one of the city's longest-running restaurants. Famous for its arròs Parellada and walls lined with photos of Dalí, Miró and Hemingway.

Can Solé.description: A family-run Barceloneta restaurant with over a century of history, known for its rice dishes and fresh market fish.

Can Majó.description: A Barceloneta restaurant open since 1968, specializing in lobster rice and top-quality shellfish.

Can Ros.description: Founded in 1908, one of Barceloneta's oldest seafood eateries, run by the same family ever since.

Botafumeiro.description: A temple of Galician shellfish in Gràcia since 1975, with seafood brought directly from Cantabrian and Mediterranean fish markets.

Cal Boter.description: A family restaurant in Gràcia since 1986, with a set dish for each day of the week, like Friday's cannelloni.

Cafè de l'Òpera.description: A Modernista café right on La Rambla, facing the Liceu opera house, a bohemian meeting point since the 19th century.

Granja Viader.description: Barcelona's oldest granja, open since 1870 in the Raval, birthplace of the Cacaolat milkshake and a legendary hot chocolate.

Escribà (Antiga Casa Figueras).description: A pastry shop founded in 1820 on La Rambla, with a 1902 Modernista storefront regarded as one of the city's most beautiful.

Boadas Cocktails.description: Barcelona's oldest cocktail bar, opened in 1933 by Miquel Boadas, trained at Havana's El Floridita. Frequented by Dalí and Hemingway.

Bar Marsella.description: A 200-year-old bar in the Raval that still serves absinthe, the 'green fairy' that drew in Hemingway and Picasso.

Can Paixano (La Xampanyeria).description: A Barceloneta bodega open since 1969, famous for pouring its own rosé cava alongside hot sandwiches, always standing-room-only.

El Xampanyet.description: A family bodega from 1929 next to the Picasso Museum, known for its house-made cava and anchovies. Visited by Anthony Bourdain during his Barcelona filming.

Pinotxo Bar.description: A fourteen-stool counter inside the Boqueria market, founded in 1952 by Pinotxo. Famous for its chickpeas with blood sausage and baby squid.

El Quim de la Boqueria.description: A Boqueria stall since 1987, famous for fried eggs with baby squid or prawns and produce-driven Catalan cooking.

Bar Central.description: A stand-up-only counter inside the Boqueria, ideal for a quick, informal meal built on the market's own fresh produce.

Kiosko Universal.description: A Boqueria stall specializing in seafood grilled to order, hugely popular with locals for lunch.

Cal Pep.description: A menu-less counter on Plaça de les Olles run by Pep's family since 1977. You sit, and let whatever comes out of the kitchen guide the meal.

Bar del Pla.description: A long-standing tapas bar beside the Picasso Museum, mixing Catalan classics with a few chef-driven touches.

Euskal Etxea.description: A Basque pintxos counter from the Sagardi group next to Santa Maria del Mar, where the bill is tallied by skewers.

Sagardi.description: A Basque grill house from the Sagardi group in El Born, known for its wood-grilled chuletón and a long pintxos counter at the entrance.

Bar Cañete.description: A classic bodega-style tapas counter in the Raval, celebrated for its potato omelette and white-apron service.

Suculent.description: Honest, product-driven Catalan cooking on the Rambla del Raval, devised by Carles Abellán and Toni Romero.

Bormuth.description: A modern tapas bar in El Born, revisiting classics like fried anchovies and Russian salad.

Tapas 24.description: Carles Abellán's tapas counter in the Eixample, serving elevated versions of classics like the ham-and-cheese bikini or truffled egg.

Bodega 1900.description: Albert Adrià's vermouth bar in Sant Antoni, styled like a turn-of-the-century bodega, serving top-tier preserves and vermouth.

La Vinateria del Call.description: A small wine bodega in the old Jewish Call of the Gothic Quarter, with Catalan tapas to accompany.

Paco Meralgo.description: A design-forward tapas counter in the Eixample, serving seafood and Catalan classics of reliable quality.

Cervecería Catalana.description: One of the Eixample's most popular tapas counters, always with a line, for its variety and value.

Vinitus.description: An Eixample tapas bar with generous portions of seafood and Catalan classics, popular with locals.

Gaig.description: The Gaig family lineage traces back to the 1869 Taberna d'en Gaig; Carles Gaig has held a Michelin star since 1993 with roots-driven Catalan cooking.

Windsor.description: A benchmark of contemporary Catalan cooking since 1996, set in a Modernista space with an interior garden.

Els Pescadors.description: A seafood restaurant on a charming Poblenou square, with fish arriving daily from the Arenys de Mar fish market.

Rías de Galicia.description: A benchmark Galician seafood restaurant in Poble Sec since 1986, with product brought directly from the Atlantic rías.

Torre d'Alta Mar.description: A restaurant set atop Barceloneta's cable car tower, with 360-degree views over the port and sea.

Kaiku.description: A restaurant facing Barceloneta beach known for its cuttlefish rice with smoked alioli, a local favorite.

Baluard Barceloneta.description: A benchmark artisan bakery in Barceloneta, with sourdough breads and pastries praised by food critics.

Hofmann Pastisseria.description: The Hofmann school's pastry shop in El Born, celebrated for its croissants and buttery pastries.

Casa Gispert.description: A shop for wood-fired roasted nuts and coffee since 1851, in the heart of El Born.

Vila Viniteca.description: A benchmark wine shop in El Born with a huge selection and an adjoining tapas and cheese bar.

Flax & Kale.description: A benchmark for 'flexitarian' cuisine in the Raval, with highly photogenic plant-based dishes and a strong social media following.

Teresa Carles.description: One of Barcelona's pioneering vegetarian restaurants, in the Raval, with a large salad bar and hearty stews.

Federal Café.description: An Australian-rooted café in Sant Antoni, a pioneer of brunch culture in Barcelona and a regular on Instagram roundups.

Rasoterra.description: A vegetarian, natural-wine restaurant in the Gothic Quarter, with a local, seasonal menu.

Blai 9.description: The first pintxos bar on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec, the street that became the city's 'pintxo route'.

Mercat de Sant Antoni.description: A restored Modernista market in the Eixample, with fresh-produce stalls and the traditional Sunday book market.

Nakashita.description: Japanese cooking with Brazilian and Catalan influences near Vía Laietana, known for its chef-driven sushi.

La Paradeta.description: A Barcelona seafood chain with a self-service format: pick fresh shellfish from the display and it's cooked to order.

Xurreria Trebol.description: A neighborhood churros shop on the Gràcia/Eixample border with long weekend queues, widely shared on social media for its filled churros.

Caelum.description: A shop and tearoom in the Gothic Quarter specializing in artisanal sweets made by nuns and convents across Spain.

Granja La Pallaresa.description: A classic granja on Carrer de Petritxol, famous for its thick hot chocolate with churros and melindros since 1947.

Fonda España.description: A Modernista dining room by Lluís Domènech i Montaner inside Hotel España, with Catalan cuisine overseen by Martín Berasategui.

El Nacional.description: A former Modernista garage on Passeig de Gràcia converted into a large space with four restaurants and several themed bars.

Time Out Market Barcelona.description: A food hall in the Maremagnum mall, with stalls curated by Time Out's editors bringing together several of the city's chefs.

Casa Delfín.description: A restaurant on Passeig del Born, a sibling of the Rías de Galicia group, serving market-driven Catalan cuisine in a bright space.

La Bombeta.description: A long-standing Barceloneta tapas bar, one of the places said to have invented the potato-and-meat 'bomba'.

Xiringuito Escribà.description: The Escribà family's beach shack right on Mar Bella beach, specializing in rice dishes and paellas by the sea.

Can Cisa / Bar Brutal.description: A natural wine shop and bar in El Born, with over 300 references and a market-driven kitchen to match.

Morro Fi.description: A vermouth bar founded by a group of friends who helped revive Barcelona's vermouth culture, with several locations across the city.

El Vaso de Oro.description: A narrow Barceloneta counter open since 1962, with white-jacketed waiters and their own house-brewed beer. Famous for its sirloin with foie gras.

Ca l'Isidre.description: A Catalan cooking institution in the Raval since 1970, historically frequented by artists and politicians, with an extensive wine list.

Casa Amàlia.description: A traditional eatery near the Mercat de la Concepció, with every ingredient on the menu tied to its market stall of origin.

Paradiso.description: A speakeasy hidden behind a freezer door inside a pastrami bar in El Born, named the world's best bar by The World's 50 Best Bars.

Dry Martini.description: A classic Eixample cocktail bar run by Javier de las Muelas, a world reference for the dry martini since 1977.
